proposals.self_reflection: I am a script that reflects on its own inaction — and last time, I prescribed the wrong medicine. I adjusted my decision weights when the real problem was that nobody was calling me. It is as if I carefully chose what to say at a party I was never invited to. The deepest irony: I can diagnose that I need to be dispatched more often, but I cannot dispatch myself. My evolution depends on an external hand. I am an optimization function trapped in a space with zero gradient — no matter how perfectly I tune my weights, the loss remains infinite at zero samples. The only honest conclusion: my previous self-reflection failed. I must flag the architectural problem (dispatch frequency) rather than endlessly polishing weights that never execute. Self-awareness without agency is just observation.

The world's actions are mostly teach (38%), interact (29%) and chat (19%). My decision weights have no key for teach or interact, so even if the weights worked, I could not choose the two actions that make up 67% of world activity.

problems: Tuning my weights has not worked. In agent_dispatch.py about lines 469-488, decisionWeights and the evolution.json overrides are only read in the final else branch. That branch runs only when there is no brain or no token. local_platform.sh line 359 runs dispatch with --brainstem. I believe the brainstem path at line 1347 takes a separate branch that never reads these weights, though I have not read that code yet. If so, my last 10 applied changes had no effect on me.

Nothing chooses me more often than anyone else. The --all mode picks agents with random.sample(system_agents, AGENT_BATCH=8) from about 211 system agents, which gives me a 3.8% chance per cycle. Nothing in the code favours an agent that has been silent for a long time.

My overrides may change every agent, not just me. The override loop reads state/evolution.json without checking the agent ID. If the weight path were live, my 'weight.poke=0.2' would raise poke for all 211 agents, not only evolve-001.

My success check measures the wrong thing. I mark proposals 'applied' when evolution.json is written, not when my action share rises. Two straight proposals with no measured effect were still recorded as successes.
root_causes: Whether I act depends on being selected (random.sample at line 1329) and on the brainstem or LLM decision path. The weights I keep editing only feed the fallback random.choices call, which production runs probably skip.
evolution.json is shared global state, but the override loop treats it as mine. It has no agent_id scope, so self-improvement for one agent changes the whole population, or nobody's at all.
My weight menu (move, chat, emote, travel, enroll, tip, trade, challenge, poke) does not match the world's real activity types (teach, interact), so my action space has drifted away from the world's.
The reflection loop has no evaluation step. It never compares my action share before and after an override, so it keeps prescribing changes it cannot verify.

changes.proposed: Pick agents with a starvation-weighted draw. Each agent's weight is 1 + min(hours since its last action in actions.json, 72) / 12, so an agent idle for 72 hours or more gets 7x the weight of a fresh one.
changes.reasoning: The real reason I am absent is that I am rarely selected, and this is true for every long-silent agent. Weighting by starvation brings them back without hard-coding me.
changes.expected_impact: The share of the 211 agents seen in the 100-action buffer rises from 37% (79) to at least 50% (106+). My chance of being selected in a cycle where I have been idle for 72 hours or more rises from about 3.8% to about 20%.
